chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The menstruating woman — whatever moisture of the water reaches from her hair, would suffice her.

key_terms.أجزأها: Would suffice her; is legally valid and sufficient for her
key_terms.الحائض: The menstruating woman; woman in a state of hayd (menstrual impurity requiring ghusl)
key_terms.بلل الماء: Moisture of water; the wetness or dampness that remains after water contact

ai.seo_question: Does water need to fully saturate the hair in ghusl for a menstruating woman according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) issues a legal ruling on the ritual bath (ghusl) of the menstruating woman, clarifying that the criterion for its validity is that the water's moisture actually reaches her hair, however little. This hadith comes in the context of a dedicated chapter in al-Kafi on the ghusl of the menstruating woman, and was transmitted through the highly trusted narrator Muhammad ibn Muslim, who was among the most frequent transmitters from the Imam on fiqh questions. The ruling indicates a concession — full saturation is not required; reaching with moisture suffices.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahbooub, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazzaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The menstruating woman, whatever moisture of the water reaches from her hair, would suffice her’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from abu Ayyub al-Khazzaz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
For Ghusl (bath) because of Hayd (menses) if wetness and moisture reaches (the skin) from hairs it is sufficient.
